Problem Statement
Real-World Broadcast Sports Vision Challenges
1. Dynamic Camera & Perspective
  • Broadcast cameras continuously pan, tilt, and zoom following the ball.
  • Perspective compression distorts distant players relative to foreground players.
  • Precludes traditional static background subtraction methods.
2. Multi-Player Occlusions
  • Players cluster in penalty boxes and cross paths during tackles and headers.
  • Standard trackers drop line-of-sight and fragment active trajectories.
  • Causes frequent identity swaps and lost tracks.
3. Sideline Personnel Interference
  • Broadcast cameras capture dugout coaches, substitutes, cameramen, and ball boys.
  • Standard detectors label everyone as 'Person', inflating counts to 26–36 individuals.
  • Pollutes match data with non-playing personnel.
4. Tracker ID Inflation
  • Trackers increment raw integer IDs (#1, #24, #58) on occlusion restarts.
  • Sports evaluators and coaches require a clean 11 vs 11 match lineup.
  • Need domain-specific tactical normalization (Goalkeeper to Striker).

Core Methodology
YOLOv8 Detection & Calibrated 78% Pitch ROI Filtering
YOLOv8 Single-Stage Detection
  • Architecture: Modified CSPDarknet backbone with C2f modules, PAN-FPN neck, and decoupled anchor-free head.
  • Target Classes: Class 0 (Player / Person) and Class 32 (Sports Ball).
  • Ground Contact Evaluation: Evaluates pitch position at bottom-center: x_ground = (x1 + x2)/2, y_ground = y2. Accurately measures player feet on grass.
  • Execution Speed: Real-time 28.4 FPS on GPU (14.2 FPS on CPU).
Calibrated 78% Pitch ROI Spatial Filter
  • The Problem: Dugout coaches and touchline cameramen sit below the pitch border, causing false player detections.
  • Mathematical Threshold: Omega_pitch = { (x,y) | 0.01W ≤ x ≤ 0.99W ∧ 0.15H ≤ y ≤ 0.78H }. Any detection with y_ground > 0.78H is pruned before tracking.
  • Empirical Measurements:
    • Deepest on-pitch player: y = 70.3% (759 px) → KEPT
    • Dugout coach: y = 87.9% (949 px) → DISCARDED
    • Cameraman: y = 93.4% (1009 px) → DISCARDED
    • Ball boy / Staff: y = 95.0% (1026 px) → DISCARDED
    • Linesman: y = 91.0% (982 px) → DISCARDED
Core Methodology
ByteTrack MOT & ResNet-18 Transfer Learning
ByteTrack Multi-Object Tracking
  • Two-Stage Bipartite Association:
    1. Associates high-score detections (conf ≥ 0.50) with Kalman predictions.
    2. Matches remaining tracklets against low-score detections (0.15 ≤ conf < 0.50).
  • Overcoming Occlusion: Retaining low-confidence boxes allows tracking through aerial headers, tackles, and multi-player crowding.
  • Motion Trajectory: Maintains rolling 30-frame feet trajectory trails for dynamic pitch visualization.
  • Occlusion Recovery Buffer: Retains lost tracks for up to 30 frames before ID termination.
ResNet-18 Transfer Learning Team Classifier
  • Upper-Torso Cropping: Bounding box slicing isolates jersey torso (y in [y1 + 0.12h, y1 + 0.55h]), excluding head/hair and legs/grass.
  • Deep Conv Features: Pretrained ResNet-18 backbone generates rich 512-dim visual embeddings: f_i in R^512.
  • Temporal Aggregation: Averages feature embeddings across frames per player ID to remove lighting artifacts.
  • K-Means Clustering (K=2): Groups player embeddings into Team White and Team Red based on relative luminance (Y = 0.299R + 0.587G + 0.114B).
Core Methodology
Tactical 22-Player Roster Normalizer
Resolving Tracker ID Inflation
  • The Problem: ByteTrack increments raw integer counters (#1, #24, #58) upon occlusion re-initialization. To sports evaluators and coaches, this looks random and confusing.
  • Algorithmic Match Selection:
    1. Partitions candidate tracks into Team White and Team Red.
    2. Ranks candidate tracks per team by frame continuity.
    3. Selects the exact top 11 active pitch players per team (11 + 11 = 22 total match players).
  • Officials Registry: Match referees, linesmen, and temporary track fragments are routed to a separate Officials & Peripheral section.
Depth-Ordered Positional Roles
  • Longitudinal Pitch Sorting: Sorts the 11 players of each team along their average pitch coordinate x from own goal line to opponent goal line:
  • Assigned Tactical Roles (Jersey #1 to #11):
    • Jersey #1: Goalkeeper (GK) — deepest position
    • Jersey #2: Right Back (RB) — defensive third
    • Jersey #3: Center Back (CB) — defensive third
    • Jersey #4: Center Back (CB) — central spine
    • Jersey #5: Left Back (LB) — defensive third
    • Jersey #6: Defensive Midfielder (CDM) — holding pivot
    • Jersey #7: Right Midfielder (RM) — flank progression
    • Jersey #8: Central Midfielder (CM) — engine room
    • Jersey #9: Striker / Center Forward (ST) — attack
    • Jersey #10: Attacking Midfielder (CAM) — playmaker
    • Jersey #11: Left Winger (LW) — attacking flank
Analytics Engine
Spatial Kinematics, 2D Pitch Heatmaps & Ball Possession
Physical Kinematics (km/h)
  • Pitch Calibration Scale: Calibrated against standard 105m pitch / 1280px canvas: s_m = 0.08203 m/px.
  • Metric Distance: d_i = s_m * sqrt(Δx^2 + Δy^2) [meters].
  • Smoothed Velocity: v_i = (d_i / Δt) * 3.6 [km/h] using a 5-frame moving average.
  • Workrate Categories:
    • ⚡ Sprinting: > 20 km/h
    • 🏃 Running: 12–20 km/h
    • 🚶 Positional Zone: < 12 km/h
2D Gaussian KDE Heatmaps
  • Bivariate KDE Formulation: Continuous spatial density modeling on pitch canvas:
    f^(x,y) = (1 / 2πσ^2N) * Σ exp(-((x-x_n)^2 + (y-y_n)^2) / 2σ^2)
    Bandwidth kernel σ = 28.0 px.
  • Three Analytical Modes:
    1. Full Match Overall Spatial Density
    2. Individual Player Tactical Corridor
    3. Team Tactical Density & Shape
Ball Possession & Formation
  • Proximity-Based Possession: Distance between ball center and player feet: k* = argmin_k ||p_ball - p_k||. Credited if distance ≤ 80px.
  • Formation Spread: Average player distance from team centroid (m). Compares wide attacking shape (>35m) vs compact defensive block (<25m).
  • Territory Area: Convex hull pitch coverage in m^2.

  • Ball Precision: 82.7% | Ball mAP@0.5: 0.791

Team Classification: ResNet-18 vs. HSV
  • Pretrained ResNet-18 (Ours): 94.8% Accuracy | 94.9% F1
  • 3D HSV Color Histogram: 82.4% Accuracy | 82.7% F1
  • Performance Gain: +12.4% Accuracy Improvement
Explainable AI: ResNet-18 Grad-CAM
  • Grad-CAM gradient activations in layer4 confirm network focuses strictly on upper-torso jersey fabric rather than grass.
  • Ensures visual representations are biologically sound and robust.
Cloud Deployment
Web Application Deployment & Interactive Features
Streamlit Cloud Architecture
  • Live Deployment: Hosted on Streamlit Community Cloud with CI/CD continuous integration linked directly to GitHub repository.
  • Linux System Dependencies: packages.txt installs FFmpeg and libGL for headless OpenCV video decoding.
  • Optimized Resource Management:
    • @st.cache_resource loads model weights once at startup
    • Stateless inference prevents memory leaks
    • Session state maintains analysis across tab switches
  • Real-Time Performance: Processes 750 frames (30s broadcast) in ~26 seconds on GPU (~28.4 FPS).
Interactive Dashboard Features
  • Full Match Source Video Preview: Review the complete broadcast video openly on the screen before analysis.
  • Pitch Boundary Cutoff Slider (65%–95%): Dynamically tune sideline staff filtering for any camera angle.
  • Analysis Duration Selector: Choose 5s (quick demo), 15s (standard tactical sequence), or 30s (full 750 frames).
  • Tactical Match Lineup Cards: Dedicated tabs for Team White (11) and Team Red (11) displaying roles, speeds, and distances.
  • One-Click IEEE Report Export: Download complete research papers in both .md and printable .html formats.

Viva Examination Q&A
  • Q: Why ByteTrack over DeepSORT?
    A: ByteTrack associates low-confidence boxes, preventing track loss during aerial duels and congestion.
  • Q: Why 78% Pitch Cutoff?
    A: Deepest pitch player is at y = 70.3%, while sideline staff are at y ≥ 87.9%. 78% provides optimal margin.
  • Q: Why ResNet-18 over HSV?
    A: HSV fails under stadium floodlight shadows; ResNet-18 captures deep textural jersey patterns.
